issues.description: Return-type annotation for simulate() in the Exercise 4 template does not match the problem statement and the solution. The problem statement (Exercise 4.6) asks students to "Simulate the circuit and return the simulation counts" (i.e. a histogram/counts mapping), and the reference solution's simulate() returns a counts dictionary (dict[str, int]). The template, however, annotates simulate() to return list[int], which contradicts both the textual instructions and the solution implementation. This mismatch can confuse students about what to return and lead to type-related test failures when comparing student output to expected counts.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the simulate() annotation and docstring in the Exercise 4 template to indicate that it should return simulation counts, i.e. a dict[str, int]. For example, update the signature to def simulate(self, qc: QuantumCircuit) -> dict[str, int]: and update the docstring to explicitly state that the function should return a counts histogram (matching the problem description and the reference solution). Ensure the template example code (if any) also demonstrates qc = qc.reverse_bits() before simulation, consistent with the instructions.
